title: The basket that remembers
scenario: A helper adds an item to a basket. A fresh basket should start EMPTY every call.

intro.job: A helper adds an item to a basket. A fresh basket should start EMPTY every call.

idea.rule: A default list is built ONCE and shared forever — defaults should be things that never change.
idea.detail: Python builds a function's default values one time, when the def line runs — not each call. A default list is therefore the same list on every call, and append keeps adding to it. The safe pattern: default to None, and build a new list inside the function.

model_restatement: Call add once per item, each time with a brand-new empty basket, and print the baskets.

clarify.question: Will callers ever pass their own basket?
clarify.answer: Sometimes — but today every call uses the default.

clarify.question: What if there are no items?
clarify.answer: Then no baskets: an empty list.

clarify.question: What should be printed?
clarify.answer: The list of baskets the calls handed back.

clarify_fallback: Good question — assume the simple case.
blueprint: Write add(item, basket) with an empty basket as the default; put the item in and hand the basket back. Call it once per item and print the baskets.
draft_code:
def add(item, basket=[]):
    basket.append(item)
    return basket
results = []
for it in items:
    results.append(add(it))
print(results)

checkpoints.prompt: After both calls — what is results?
With the fix — after both calls, what is results?

why_line: basket=[] was built once, when def ran — both calls append to that same list, so both entries in results are the one list ['pen', 'mug'].

explain.rule: The default basket is a single shared basket by the door — the second shopper picks up the one with the pen still in it, and both receipts point at the same basket.
explain.bridge: So how could each call get a brand-new basket instead of the one by the door?

fix.rule: Default to None and build the list inside: basket = [] then runs on every call, so every call gets its own.

walk.gloss: No basket given? The default is None — nothing shared.
Check whether a basket was passed in.
If not, build a brand-new empty one — this runs every call.
Add the item to this call's own basket.

hints: After the second call, look at results[0]. Did it change?
The [] in the def line is built once, not once per call.
Use basket=None, then basket = [] inside when it's None.

follow_up.fix_hint: The baskets should stay separate — if both lists show ['a', 'a'], the calls shared one basket.

one_liner: A default list is built ONCE and shared forever — defaults should be things that never change.
